tictactoe.title: Tic-Tac-Toe · {size}×{size}
tictactoe.subtitle: Complete a line of {need} marks before your opponent does.
tictactoe.turn_text: Players take turns placing ✕ and ○ in empty cells on the {size}×{size} board. One turn means one mark.
tictactoe.win_text: Be the first to place {need} of your marks in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
tictactoe.win_tip: On a {size}×{size} board, the winning line is {need} marks in a row.
tictactoe.draw_text: If every cell is filled and neither player has a winning line, the match ends in a draw.
tictactoe.diagram_label: {size}×{size} board: example of a winning line of {need} marks
tictactoe.diagram_caption: Example winning line: {need} in a row

four_in_a_row.title: Four in a Row · {columns}×{rows}
four_in_a_row.subtitle: Connect four of your pieces in one line before your opponent does.
four_in_a_row.turn_text: Choose a column on the {columns}×{rows} board. Your piece drops into the lowest empty cell in that column.
four_in_a_row.win_text: Be the first to connect {connect} pieces horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
four_in_a_row.size_text: This match uses a {columns}×{rows} board. The board size can vary, but every variant is won by connecting {connect} pieces.
four_in_a_row.draw_text: If the {columns}×{rows} board is completely filled and nobody connects four pieces, the match ends in a draw.
four_in_a_row.tip: 💡 Build your own line, but watch your opponent’s threats — sometimes blocking a column in time matters more.

reversi.title: Reversi · {size}×{size}
reversi.subtitle: Flip your opponent’s pieces and finish with the majority.
reversi.size_text: This match uses a {size}×{size} board. The basic rules are the same for 6×6, 8×8, and 10×10.
reversi.start_text: Four pieces begin diagonally in the center of the {size}×{size} board. Sides are assigned at random, and Black always moves first.
reversi.legal_text: Place a piece so that a continuous line of your opponent’s pieces lies between the new piece and one of your existing pieces. Legal cells are highlighted.
reversi.flip_text: All trapped opponent pieces flip to your color. Horizontal, vertical, and diagonal lines are checked.
reversi.multi_text: A single move can flip several lines at once. Every opponent piece enclosed by your pieces after the new placement flips immediately.
reversi.pass_text: If you have no legal moves, the system automatically passes the turn to your opponent. You cannot voluntarily pass when a legal move is available.
reversi.finish_text: The game ends when the board is full or neither player has a legal move. The player with more pieces wins. If the score is tied, the result is a draw and the entry fee is refunded.
reversi.timer_text: You have 60 seconds per turn. Leaving an active game or running out of time results in a technical loss.
reversi.diagram_label: Example Reversi rule on a {size}×{size} board

go.title: Go · {size}×{size}
go.subtitle: Surround enemy stones and claim territory.
go.size_text: This match uses a {size}×{size} board. The rules are the same for 9×9 and 13×13; only the board size and game length change.
go.start_text: The game begins on an empty {size}×{size} board. Stones are placed on line intersections and do not move afterward. Sides are assigned at random, and Black moves first.
go.liberties_text: Horizontally or vertically adjacent stones of the same color form a group. Empty adjacent intersections are its liberties. Diagonal stones are not connected.
go.capture_text: If an opponent’s stone or group has no liberties left, the entire group is removed from the board. One move can capture several groups.
go.suicide_text: You cannot place a stone if your own group would have no liberties. The move is allowed if it first captures opposing stones and frees intersections.
go.ko_text: You cannot immediately recreate a board position that has already occurred in the game. After a reciprocal capture, you must first play somewhere else.
go.pass_text: You may pass at any time. Two consecutive passes end the game. Before the second pass, the game asks you to confirm that you want to finish.
go.score_text: You score one point for every stone on the board and every surrounded empty intersection. Mixed areas are neutral. White receives {komi} komi points because Black moves first. All stones remaining after the second pass are considered alive.
go.timer_text: You have 60 seconds per turn. Leaving an active game or running out of time results in a technical loss.
go.diagram_label: Example Go rule on a {size}×{size} board

checkers.title: Russian Checkers
checkers.subtitle: Capture all of your opponent’s pieces or leave them with no legal move.
checkers.board_text: The game is played on an 8×8 board. Each player starts with 12 pieces. Moves are made only on dark squares.
checkers.move_text: A regular piece moves one empty square diagonally forward.
checkers.capture_text: If an opponent’s piece can be captured, you cannot make a regular move. A regular piece may capture both forward and backward.
checkers.chain_text: If the same piece can capture again after the first capture, you must continue with that piece. If several capture paths are available, you may choose any of them.
checkers.king_text: A piece becomes a king when it reaches the last row. A king can move any number of empty squares diagonally. When capturing, it jumps over an opponent’s piece and may land on any legal empty square farther along the diagonal.
checkers.promotion_text: If a piece reaches the last row during a capture sequence, it becomes a king immediately and continues the same sequence as a king.
checkers.win_text: Capture all of your opponent’s pieces or leave them with no legal move. Repeatedly returning to the same position may result in a draw.

chess.title: Chess
chess.subtitle: Checkmate your opponent’s king.
chess.start_text: The classic 8×8 board is used. Sides are assigned at random, and White moves first.
chess.pawn_text: Moves one square forward, or two from its starting position. Captures diagonally. En passant is available.
chess.lines_text: The rook moves along ranks and files, the bishop moves diagonally, and the queen combines both. They cannot jump over pieces.
chess.knight_text: Moves in an L shape and is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.
chess.check_text: The king cannot be left under attack. If the king is in check and there are no legal moves to escape it, that is checkmate.
chess.castle_text: The king and rook may move together if neither has moved, the squares between them are empty, and the king does not move through an attacked square.
chess.promotion_text: When a pawn reaches the last rank, it promotes to a queen, rook, bishop, or knight. The player chooses the piece.
chess.draw_text: A draw can result from stalemate, insufficient material, threefold repetition, or 50 moves by each player without a pawn move or capture.
chess.timer_text: You have 60 seconds per turn. Leaving an active game or running out of time results in a technical loss.

domino.title: Domino
domino.subtitle: Match equal numbers and be the first to play all your tiles.
domino.start_text: Each player receives 7 tiles, and the rest stay face down in the stock. The highest double is placed automatically, then the second player moves.
domino.match_text: You may place a tile at either end of the chain if one of its numbers matches the open number.
domino.side_text: If a tile can be played at either end, select the tile first, then tap one of the two highlighted positions on the table.
domino.doubles_text: Tiles with matching numbers are placed across the chain. Playing a double does not grant an extra turn.
domino.draw_text: If you have no playable tile, tap “Draw”. Each tap draws one tile. If it still cannot be played, tap “Draw” again. When the stock is empty, your turn is passed automatically.
domino.win_text: You win by playing your last tile. If nobody can move and the stock is empty, the lower pip total wins. Equal totals result in a draw.
domino.timer_text: You have 60 seconds per turn. Leaving an active game or running out of time results in a technical loss.

battleship.title: Battleship
battleship.subtitle: Sink your opponent’s entire fleet before they destroy yours.
battleship.fleet_text: Place 10 ships on the 10×10 board, occupying 20 cells in total.
battleship.placement_text: Choose a ship and tap the required number of adjacent cells in a straight line. Ships cannot overlap or touch, even diagonally.
battleship.setup_time_text: You can use “Randomize fleet” as many times as you like, or place ships manually. If time runs out, ships already placed stay where they are and the system adds only the missing ships.
battleship.shot_text: Choose a cell on your opponent’s board. A miss passes the turn. After a hit or sinking a ship, you shoot again.
battleship.timer_text: The timer restarts after every shot. If your turn timer expires, the match is recorded as a technical loss.
battleship.win_text: Be the first to destroy all 10 of your opponent’s ships.

rules_guide.title: How regular matches work
rules_guide.subtitle: A quick guide to matchmaking, coins, wins, draws, and match history.
rules_guide.start_text_1: Choose a game on the Home screen, configure the available options, and start searching for an opponent. Coins are not deducted while you are searching. The entry fee is charged only when a match is actually created.
rules_guide.start_text_2: The system first tries to find another player with compatible settings. If no suitable player is found for a while, a bot may become your opponent in regular matchmaking.
rules_guide.start_text_3: To play with a specific person, open {friends}, find them by nickname or MGW-ID, open the {more} menu, and choose {invite}.
rules_guide.cost_text: Each player pays {entry} to enter. The total pot for a regular match is therefore currently {pot}.
rules_guide.cost_example: For example, under the current terms, the winner gets their entry fee back together with the winnings: {winner_reward} is credited to the balance. The winner’s net result compared with the balance before the match is {winner_net}.
rules_guide.win_text: {label} the winner receives {winner_reward} from the total pot, while {commission} is the system fee.
rules_guide.loss_text: {label} the entry fee for this match is not refunded.
rules_guide.draw_text: {label} each player gets their entry fee back — currently {draw_refund}. There is no fee on a draw.
rules_guide.leave_title: 4. Do not leave an unfinished match
rules_guide.leave_text: If a match has already started and you leave it manually before it ends, the app will warn you about the consequences. Leaving may count as a technical loss, so it is better to finish the game or return after a temporary connection drop.
rules_guide.game_rules_text: Each game has its own rules, board sizes, and available variants. Before a match or from the game interface, open {rules} to see the rules for the selected game. This section explains the general rules for regular matches and coins.
rules_guide.history_text: The {more} menu includes {balance_history} and {match_history}. There you can review entry deductions, draw refunds, win rewards, and your latest played matches.
rules_guide.bonus_text: The current weekly free-bonus terms are shown separately on the balance card. Use {weekly_bonus} to view the current conditions.
rules_guide.tournaments_text: Tournaments are a separate mode with their own registration, match, and reward rules. The regular-match rules in this window do not replace the rules of a specific tournament.
rules_guide.problems_text: If your balance, match result, or another action looks wrong, open {more_feedback}. To report another player, use the separate {report} item.
